title: Denying Self
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Denying self means surrendering self-rule, pride, sinful desire, and personal control in order to follow Jesus Christ. It is the daily refusal to make self the lord, savior, and center of life.
summary: Denying self means surrendering self-rule, pride, sinful desire, and personal control in order to follow Jesus Christ. It is the daily refusal to make self the lord, savior, and center of life.
christFocus: Jesus Christ denied Himself in perfect obedience to the Father and gave Himself for sinners. His self-giving love becomes both the ground and pattern of the believer’s surrender.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Denying self does not mean despising the dignity God gives to people made in His image. It means refusing the sinful self-rule that wants life apart from Christ. The disciple no longer belongs to himself but to the Lord who bought him.

Jesus connects self-denial with following Him. The way of Christ cannot be walked while the old self remains enthroned. Pride, control, comfort, approval, sinful desire, and personal ambition must all bow before the Lord.

This surrender is not loss in the deepest sense. Whoever loses his life for Christ’s sake finds true life. Denying self frees believers from the tyranny of self and brings them into the joy of belonging wholly to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Self-rule often disguises itself as freedom, but it becomes bondage. People can be enslaved to image, comfort, fear, control, desire, or the approval of others while still using spiritual language.

This doctrine calls believers away from a self-centered Christianity. Christ does not merely improve personal plans; He becomes Lord over the whole person.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your desires, plans, fears, ambitions, and need for control before Christ. Ask where self-rule is resisting His lordship. Surrender what He exposes, trust His goodness, and practice daily obedience even when it costs comfort, pride, or approval.
